A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Unisolver research, with matching authors, architecture and principal benchmarks. Their readable text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: v3 reports original HeterNS simulations and neural-solver evaluations, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, fine-tuning, generalization and scalability results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds encoding ablations, joint-training comparisons, longer-trajectory evaluation and inference-efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The component encoders, LLaMA-3 embeddings, domain-wise/point-wise subspace division and scale/shift/select conditioning remain unchanged. v3 Equation (3) matches v4 Equation (2). Additional implementation explanations and experimental variants do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: The three benchmark families and PDEBench transfer tasks remain. v4 Appendix I.3 adds temporal extrapolation on HeterNS to 30-second trajectories, beyond the 20 seconds represented during training. The joint-training study partitions existing 1D PDE coverage rather than introducing another PDE family.

E2.justification: v4 Table 22 adds the pseudo-spectral numerical solver as an evaluated timing and memory comparator. The corresponding retained accuracy comparisons preserve their neural baselines, including PDEformer and DPOT; Factformer/FactFormer is a spelling change.

E3.justification: New protocols include joint versus independent training on three disjoint 10,000-sample polynomial subsets for 500 epochs, 30-second trajectory evaluation, and per-frame efficiency measurement on an A100 with batch size one. v4 also introduces configuration-averaged HeterNS reporting. Existing benchmark training configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix A tests term-count, incorrect-expression and handcrafted encodings; Appendix C.1 tests joint versus independent training; Appendices I.3 and I.5 examine temporal extrapolation and efficiency. The polynomial-order fine-tuning and double-unseen viscosity/force analyses already existed in v3 and are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix G.5 and v4 Appendix I.6 report the same three HeterNS repetitions, standard deviations and confidence claims. The corresponding uncertainty tables retain their values, and the added experiments introduce no reported seed or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Main benchmark values are retained, while supplementary results are added, including 30-second errors of 0.1956 for Unisolver versus 0.2527 for ViT. Figure 7(b) replaces duplicated viscosity 5e-4 results with 5e-5 results. The headline force-generalization gain changes from 43.9% to 66.7% through aggregation of retained scores, not improved same-setting predictions.

T1.justification: The analytical string-vibration solution moves to v4 Appendix F, but v3 Appendix D's detailed derivation, extension definitions, Lemmas 2–3 and proofs are removed. v4 instead directs readers to Evans or other books. This substantially reduces the supplied formal reasoning while retaining the motivating solution.

C1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction frame universality as a goal through 'Towards' and 'aiming towards,' softening v3's presentation of an achieved universal solver. The conditioning architecture, complete-component contributions and state-of-the-art claims across three benchmarks remain.

C2.justification: v4 Appendix A explicitly distinguishes useful mathematical information in LLM embeddings from demonstrating that an LLM understands mathematics. Appendix H.2 adds a rationale for component-presence masks alongside LLM embeddings. The grid-data limitation and proposed irregular-mesh future work were already present in v3.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code link, changes the HeterNS data-access link and removes the supplementary-video pointer. It newly specifies one-step training with autoregressive evaluation, orthogonal random-vector controls, and masking/incomplete-input details. These clarify existing experiments without establishing that their procedures changed or were rerun.

R1.justification: v4 removes the OFormer and latent spectral model discussions and references, plus the Stein–Shakarchi book reference. The string-equation explanation instead cites the already-listed Evans textbook. The broader positioning relative to PINNs, neural operators and PDE-conditioned solvers remains.

P1.justification: The title and abstract are revised, several passages are condensed, and model-analysis paragraphs and appendices are reordered. Generalization studies are collected earlier and trajectory visualizations move later. The five main sections and most methodological and benchmark exposition remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The main text adopts a two-column conference layout. v4 adds a task-overview figure, redraws the architecture and PCA displays, revises Figure 7, and transposes Tables 1–2. Detailed HeterNS tables move to the appendix while a new aggregate table replaces them in the main text.

improvement.justification: The new encoding controls test alternative explanations for LLM benefits, while joint-training, temporal-extrapolation and efficiency studies strengthen practical support. More cautious universality and LLM interpretations, plus clearer implementation information, improve transparency. Main benchmark conclusions remain unchanged. Removing the detailed string-equation proof reduces self-containedness, although the analytical result and attribution remain; the net improvement is limited.
